channel.description: Noticias de ciencia de todas las fuentes configuradas.

item.title: ‘Still standing’: king jokes as he appears on Elton John’s Rocket Hour
item.description: Charles marks 78th birthday and 50th anniversary of King’s Trust charity with a playlist for special episode of podcast King Charles marked his 78th birthday on Saturday joking with Elton John that they were “still standing” as he appeared on the singer-songwriter’s Rocket Hour for a shared musical journey. In a special recorded episode of the Apple Radio show to mark the 50th anniversary of the monarch’s charity the King’s Trust, Charles’s playlist included John’s I’m Still Standing. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Davies

item.title: Michigan Dad Pauses Fundraiser: viral prank target stops at $784,273; urges gifts to others
item.description: Walter Zerod, a delivery worker who faced a shocking prank at work, found unexpected financial relief through a GoFundMe campaign that skyrocketed to nearly $785,000. This overwhelming support not only helped him but also highlighted the kindness of strangers. In a selfless move, Zerod chose to pause further donations, encouraging his supporters to extend their generosity to other families in financial hardship, demonstrating his deep appreciation and desire for privacy. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: En 2004 el PSOE dio un vuelco electoral. Automáticamente los científicos notaron algo: un cambio en los embarazos y las bodas
item.description: Cuando una pareja decide tener hijos valora cuestiones como su estabilidad laboral, el precio de vivienda , si tendrá o no apoyo familiar ( benditos abuelos ) o la marcha de la economía , pero… ¿Entra la política en esa ecuación? ¿Pueden influir unas elecciones en la demografía de un territorio, alterando, aunque sea brevemente, la natalidad, la tasa de abortos y el número de enlaces? Un estudio realizado por investigadores de la Universitat de Barcelona (UB), la Pompeu Fabra (UPF) y Cambra de Barcelona cree que sí. Y mucho. Al menos esa es la conclusión que han sacado al analizar las… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Prego

item.title: SpaceX's Starship soars into orbit after booster explosion prevents an unprecedented double catch
item.description: SpaceX's attempt to recover its entire Starship back at the launch pad was thwarted when the booster fell into the Gulf of Mexico and exploded Friday, but the spacecraft still soared into orbit in its boldest test yet. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Los científicos coinciden: las personas más inteligentes son también las más solitarias por culpa de la evolución
item.description: “Tan listo para unas cosas y tan tonto para otras”. Lo que podría ser el tópico espetado a un niño prodigio cuando se le ve fallar en operaciones tan simples como el saber relacionarse con otros niños en el patio de colegio, puede tener en el fondo parte de razón; y lo que es más, raíces biológicas heredadas de siglos y siglos de ancestros. Esto es lo que dice la ciencia sobre los inteligentes tristes y solitarios. Mejor solo que neciamente acompañado: en 2016 dos investigadores publicaron en el British Journal of Psychology un concienzudo análisis sobre más de 15.000 sujetos y cuyos… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Esther Miguel Trula

item.title: Chinese scientists fired after child dies in world’s first brain gene-editing attempt
item.description: The world’s first attempt to edit genes inside a child’s brain, which killed a six-year-old girl in Shanghai last year, has led to the firing of scientists following an official investigation that found they had broken research rules and taken money from her family. The investigation, ordered by the Communist Party’s Shanghai municipal committee and the local government, concluded on Friday that the researchers had not shared worrying results from monkey tests with the girl’s doctors beforehand.... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Ling Xin

item.title: Yale scientists reveal what really slows aging and what doesn't
item.description: Yale researchers have discovered that certain prescription drugs, healthy diets, and exercise can measurably slow biological aging, while popular anti-aging supplements appear largely ineffective. Their analysis of 51 studies could transform how scientists evaluate anti-aging treatments, although whether these biological changes actually extend life remains uncertain. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: 5,000-year-old skulls reveal a disturbing secret of ancient Egypt's first kings
item.description: A 5,000-year-old mystery surrounding the tombs of Egypt’s first kings has taken a disturbing turn. Scientists reexamining 46 ancient skulls discovered evidence of potentially fatal head injuries in 18, suggesting that at least 39% of those studied may have been deliberately killed. The findings support a century-old theory that royal attendants were sacrificed when kings died, possibly to serve them in the afterlife. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: The role of social relationships in scaling agricultural innovations: A dimension that remains underreported in research
item.description: A study published in Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems reveals that, although partnerships and institutional collaboration feature prominently in climate-oriented agricultural research, their relationship with the scaling of innovations is rarely explicitly documented. The findings highlight the need to better understand the role of social relationships to strengthen the design, monitoring and evaluation of scaling processes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX launches Starship rocket, fails to recover booster
item.description: SpaceX had planned to catch and later reuse both stages of its biggest rocket for the first time. But the booster exploded over the Gulf of Mexico, while the spacecraft continued into orbit. Fuente: Deutsche Welle - World.

item.title: Forcing yourself to smile can actually make you miserable
item.description: Smiling may not always make you happier, and new research suggests that forcing yourself to smile repeatedly could actually make you feel worse. In a University of Florida study involving more than 1,100 participants, researchers discovered that while a single artificial smile can provide a small mood boost, repeatedly faking smiles can erase that benefit or even reverse it. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Heavier-than-expected electron behavior may explain slower electrical flow in alpha-gallium oxide
item.description: Power electronic devices help control the flow of electricity and convert it into forms needed by different machines, such as electric vehicles, renewable energy systems and industrial equipment. Some electrical energy is lost as heat during this process, reducing efficiency and potentially affecting the device's performance. Semiconductor materials that can withstand high voltages, carry electricity efficiently and release heat effectively would make these devices more efficient and reliable. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX launches Starship in key test flight of massive rocket
item.description: The test flight is SpaceX's first attempt to ​catch both the Super Heavy booster and upper stage spacecraft of the rocket at its launch site in Starbase, Texas. Fuente: CNBC - World.

item.title: Scientists capture electrons making seemingly impossible quantum jumps
item.description: Scientists have captured electrons making seemingly impossible jumps across forbidden energy gaps in graphene, with some transitions occurring at a remarkable 100% probability. The breakthrough offers an unprecedented look at quantum behavior and could help unlock a new generation of ultrafast, light-controlled electronics. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Christina Koch, la primera mujer en viajar alrededor de la Luna: “Veíamos destellos azules cuando cerrábamos los ojos”
item.description: Tras completar con éxito el histórico sobrevuelo lunar, se conoció una frase que la astronauta de la NASA pronunció mientras realizaba la misión Artemis II Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
item.description: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: AI supercharges laser physics with a stunning 250x speed boost
item.description: Researchers at Stanford, UCLA, and SLAC have developed an AI system that simulates complex laser interactions thousands of times faster than conventional methods. The breakthrough allows scientists to predict how laser pulses behave inside special crystals in just milliseconds, without sacrificing much accuracy. This could dramatically improve the precision and efficiency of powerful X-ray lasers used in cutting-edge scientific research. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Fiji petrel eludes 10-day search as communities aim to protect bird's habitat
item.description: A new study details scientists' search for one of the planet's rarest birds in the waters off Fiji's Gau Island. Spanning 10 days, the expedition yielded no verified sightings of the critically endangered Fiji petrel, one of the world's most elusive birds. Fewer than 50 individuals are believed to remain on Earth. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX’s bid for Starship double catch thwarted, as booster ends up in ocean
item.description: SpaceX launched Starship towards orbit on Friday in its boldest test yet: a 22-hour flight that aimed to capture the entire rocket in a move meant to accelerate moon and Mars travel. But Elon Musk’s company had to lower its expectations when the first part of the double catch flopped. The first-stage booster malfunctioned and instead of returning to its Texas pad several minutes after lift-off, it ended up in the Gulf of Mexico after an automatic abort. Despite the setback, the bullet-shaped... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Associated Press

item.title: Unstable plasma heats itself with waves it generates, experiments reveal
item.description: Fusion power is expected to be a sustainable energy source that emits no carbon dioxide during electricity generation. To achieve this, research is underway worldwide to confine high-temperature plasma using magnetic fields. To initiate a fusion reaction, high-energy particles or waves must be injected from outside to heat the plasma to extremely high temperatures. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rob Roy MacGregor’s gravestone;scans suggest first carvings were made 1,000years before he died
item.description: A recent study has uncovered that the gravestone of Rob Roy MacGregor, found at Balquhidder Parish Church, has roots that stretch back an astonishing thousand years prior to his life. Utilizing 3D imaging techniques, researchers have discovered that the stone features carvings from multiple eras, hinting at a potential connection to early medieval Christianity through its intricate designs. For those intrigued, digital models have been made publicly accessible for exploration. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Same farms, different answers: When nitrogen pollution estimates don't add up
item.description: To reduce nitrogen pollution stemming from synthetic fertilizer and livestock waste, California's Central Valley relies on five data sets to estimate surplus nitrogen. However, most parts of the United States use just one or two data sets—the U.S. Department of Agriculture's agricultural survey and census—to estimate nitrogen surplus. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hidden 'master switch' allows bacteria to breach the body's defenses
item.description: Researchers at Penn Dental Medicine have uncovered a previously unknown molecular mechanism by which bacteria rapidly compromise the body's protective barriers, a finding that could reshape how scientists approach a wide range of serious diseases. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Planimal' cells retain nearly entire algal genome after experimental cell fusion
item.description: Most DNA in an organism is inherited from its parent or parents. This form of genetic inheritance is referred to as vertical inheritance because genes are passed down from generation to generation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Modified $450 3D printer builds living materials with more than 100 layers
item.description: Living materials created with a 3D printer are like living tissues with one notable exception: You get to choose exactly which cells are in them, as well as their final 3D shape. Depending on the type of bacteria included in the print, the material can clean up contaminated water or break down waste materials such as plastic. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Genomic analysis restores species status to 12 overlooked Great Barrier Reef corals
item.description: An international team of scientists working with Queensland Museum's CoralBank project has uncovered previously hidden coral diversity on Australia's east coast, revealing that 12 corals once considered variations of other species are distinct species in their own right. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Common ADHD classroom accommodations may not help students succeed, study finds
item.description: Extra time on assignments. Frequent breaks. A quiet place to work. For students with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), these are some of the most common accommodations schools provide to make learning easier. But are they actually helping children succeed? A new study from Florida International University (FIU) suggests that some widely used approaches may be falling short. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Happy face, angry voice: Human–dog interaction study tracks conflicting cues
item.description: Dogs, having lived alongside humans for tens of thousands of years, are keenly tuned in to our emotions. Behavioral experiments, brain studies and even measurements of heart rate all suggest dogs respond differently depending on the emotional expressions they encounter in humans. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A perfect couple: Chromium keeps ruthenium grounded in water electrolysis
item.description: They say opposites attract, and many couples do fit this pattern. One is pragmatic and down-to-earth, while the other is a dreamer with their head in the clouds. Yet, these differences make them perfect for each other. According to researchers at ICFO, chemical interactions between atoms are not that different. Ruthenium, for instance, belongs to the "dreamer" class. It is commonly used in single-atom catalysts that speed up water electrolysis, which splits water to obtain green hydrogen. However, on its own, ruthenium tends to over-oxidize and dissolve during operation, like an idealist who… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Most people dislike coffee at first and learn to love it, and scientists now say the reason may be a slow dopamine signal from the gut that teaches the brain to like flavours linked with calories, even bitter ones
item.description: Researchers have discovered that our tastes for certain foods, even those that might initially be bitter, shift as we grow. The gut sends vital signals to our brain about what we eat, influencing our cravings through dopamine, which is known for its role in reward and motivation. Consequently, this insight provides a fascinating explanation for why we often learn to appreciate flavors such as coffee. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: A newly discovered South African dinosaur was a heavyweight even as a youngster
item.description: It probably walked on two legs and weighed about 400 kilograms (880 pounds), despite still being a youngster. Meet Nyana rooiwalensis, a newly identified dinosaur species that lived more than 200 million years ago in what is now South Africa. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Indian-origin family in Canada seeks $5.5 million for US gene therapy they hope will help their toddler with rare genetic disorder
item.description: Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: Poulomi Ghosh

item.title: El USB del espacio: Europa crea un conector universal para reparar satélites en órbita en lugar de tirarlos
item.description: ¿Te imaginas que tu móvil se queda sin batería o te da el más mínimo fallo, lo tiras a la basura y te compras otro? Básicamente eso es lo que se hace con los satélites en el espacio. Cuando se quedan sin combustible o sufren algún daño , generalmente se abandonan y se sustituyen, de modo que el viejo pasa a engrosar las filas de la basura espacial. Lo ideal sería enviar naves capaces de transmitir energía, datos, calor y otros recursos necesarios para reparar los satélites, de modo que puedan seguir usándose. Sin embargo, eso requiere el uso de conectores compatibles tanto con el satélite… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Molecular sensor makes invisible traces of mercury easier to see
item.description: Mercury contamination presents an obvious challenge: it is invisible. A glass of water or a piece of fruit can seem perfectly normal to the naked eye, even when trace amounts of toxic mercury are present. Detecting such minute levels usually requires specialized laboratory tools and trained experts. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hallan enterrado vivo en una jaula a un bebé después de que su padre se lo llevara
item.description: Después de más de 24 horas desaparecido, las autoridades de la Oficina del sheriff del condado de Lexington ( Estados Unidos ) han rescatado al pequeño Koah Sharpe, un bebé de 11 meses que había sido enterrado vivo dentro de una jaula para perros cubierta por una toalla. El responsable es presuntamente el padre del pequeño, que fue detenido por varioas cargos la noche previa al salvamento del niño.Un despliegue de cerca de 100 agentes localizó al bebé sepultado a una profundidad de 30 centímetros en los bosques de Carolina del Sur próximos a la casa de su abuela paterna. Los investigadores… Fuente: ABC España - Internacional.
item.dc:creator: África Albalá

item.title: Fruit fly sleep protein yields peptides that inhibit drug-resistant bacteria in lab tests
item.description: Researchers at University of Tsukuba and collaborating institutions have identified short antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri, a sleep-inducing protein in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster. The research is published in the journal Nature Communications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New genetic atlas reveals traces of 10,000 years of sheep breeding
item.description: For around 10,000 years, humans have selectively bred sheep for desirable traits. Generation after generation, we have chosen animals for their wool, size and reproductive characteristics and gradually left our mark on their DNA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient rocks reveal a dramatic journey from deep inside Earth
item.description: Surface rocks can reveal records of regions they occupied millions of years ago, even if those areas were kilometers below ground. On Türkiye's Marmara Sea's southern shores and islands, granitic rocks that are now exposed originated as molten material deep in Earth's crust. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Evolution found another way to build a primate brain
item.description: What makes the human brain so much larger and more complex than the brains of many other mammals? Scientists have long sought clues in our DNA. Some discoveries show how genetic changes enable the developing brain to produce more cells. Others help explain how long those cells can continue to multiply. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mountain growth spurts may have sparked complex life on Earth
item.description: Mountain ranges grew higher throughout Earth's history in two distinct "spurts" that correlated with the flourishing of biological diversity on our planet, according to new research published in the journal Science Advances. The study suggests mountains may have played a key role in sparking complex life. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A likely supermassive neutron star might shed light on the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes
item.description: A team of astronomers recently identified a red giant star with an unseen binary companion after examining data from the Large Sky Area MultiObject Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE). Although the companion object can't be observed visually, astronomers can see the gravitational effects it has on the red giant star. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ocean absorbs more fossil fuel carbon while land uptake stalls, 30 years of data show
item.description: The ocean has been absorbing carbon dioxide from fossil fuel emissions at an increasing rate since 1990, while the net uptake of carbon by forests, soils and other land ecosystems has not grown, according to a new study led by scientists at UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Combining five metals in one oxide improves ethanol gas sensing
item.description: A technology that significantly improves ethanol gas sensing performance by combining five different metal elements in a single oxide has been developed. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Water-activated polymer forms solid shapes underwater and bonds glass fragments
item.description: Cement hardens when mixed with water, allowing it to form solid structures even in wet environments. This property is known as hydraulicity. Reproducing this property in organic polymers has been challenging, as polymer materials that react with moisture often lack the combination of bulk curing and water resistance needed to harden reliably in wet conditions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Who lives in a sponge under the sea? Tiny Caribbean fish and their microscopic neighbors
item.description: Two new studies involving Newcastle University marine scientist Dr. Theresa Rueger have highlighted how the tusked goby's relationship with its host sponge shapes almost every aspect of its life. Rueger, a senior lecturer in tropical marine sciences at Newcastle University's School of Natural and Environmental Sciences, is senior author of one study and co-author of the other, which together uncover the influence of sponges on the tiny Caribbean reef fish's social behavior, growth, reproduction and microbiome. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: From stimulation to suppression: How nitrogen addition changes soil respiration over time
item.description: Soil respiration (Rs), the efflux of CO₂ from soils to the atmosphere driven by root and microbial activity, is one of the largest terrestrial carbon fluxes and a primary determinant of net carbon sequestration. The important role of nitrogen in driving terrestrial carbon sequestration has long been recognized. However, the role of nitrogen in the temporal dynamics of Rs has not been well understood. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Timing of Climate Science Reports Ignites a Hot Fight at U.N. Talks
item.description: Several countries that rely heavily on fossil fuels want to delay the next round of scientific assessments that governments use to inform their climate policies. Fuente: The New York Times - World.
item.dc:creator: Chico Harlan and Lisa Friedman

item.title: How Chinese brewers refined their booze 5,000 years ago
item.description: More than 5,000 years ago, brewers in eastern China appear to have used red mold to make rice alcohol, then strained the drink through cloth. Microscopic residues on ancient pottery show evidence of both the fermentation method and the filtering process to separate the liquid from leftover grain. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Kindergarten teachers offer cognitive help during outdoor play but fall short on emotional and social support
item.description: A study in the International Journal of Innovation and Sustainable Development of teachers' behavior during outdoor play at kindergarten has identified a gap between the support children need and the help educators provide, particularly in emotional and social development. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Self-learning AI separates particle jets from background noise in simulated heavy-ion collisions
item.description: A team of physicists and computer scientists led by researchers at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Brookhaven National Laboratory developed a new artificial intelligence (AI) approach that learns on its own to separate important high-energy particle jet signals from the enormous background of particles recorded in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, where two beams of heavy ions collide at near the speed of light. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: As EU grapples with fierce AI competition, summit overshadowed by elusive Ukraine-Russia peace deal
item.description: As EU leaders meet for an AI summit in Dublin, largely overshadowed by Russia's war on Ukraine, William Hilderbrandt is pleased to welcome Fabrice Pothier, CEO of Rasmussen Global. On AI, Pothier points to Europe's limited computing capacity, estimating that it barely represents "5% of what's available out there." Despite the EU's wealth of researchers and expertise, he warns that Europe is struggling to turn these resources into "real technological and industrial scale." Now, turning to the war in Ukraine, Pothier argues that European governments should focus less on "whether they have a… Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Colorful fish reveal how species stay distinct despite interbreeding
item.description: Vividly colored fish dwelling at the bottom of shallow Midwestern streams may help biologists understand the evolutionary mechanisms by which species remain distinct despite their similarities and overlapping ranges. Orangethroat and rainbow darters regularly interbreed where their ranges overlap, yet—millions of years after they first diverged—they remain separate species. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rh₃ clusters balance activity and butene selectivity in butane dehydrogenation
item.description: Scientists from the Institute of Metal Research (IMR) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, in collaboration with researchers from Peking University and Chongqing University, have demonstrated how the geometry and electronic properties of subnanometer rhodium (Rh) active sites shape C–H activation, product desorption and C–C bond cleavage during butane dehydrogenation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hallan en Asturias un diente de un tiburón superdepredador gigante de hace 331 millones de años
item.description: La primera vez que estuve allí me dijeron que en Covadonga se mira para arriba, es decir, a la estructura superior de la basílica neogótica. Bueno, y al techo de la Santa Cueva. Pero esta vez el hallazgo ha llegado por mirar hacia abajo, porque un equipo de geólogos ha dado con un diente fósil incrustado en una losa de caliza roja junto al Santuario. Y al parecer es de un enorme tiburón (entre 5 y 6 metros) que nadaba por la zona hace 331 millones de años, mucho antes de que los dinosaurios se plantearan existir o extinguirse. El hallazgo. Un equipo compuesto por profesionales de lav… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Isra Fdez

item.title: Heat drives electron orbital currents, revealing first experimental evidence of orbital Nernst effect
item.description: Researchers at National Taiwan University (NTU) have reported the first experimental evidence of heat-current-driven transverse accumulation of electrons' orbital angular momentum, a phenomenon known as the orbital Nernst effect. The study was recently published in Nature Communications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists successfully swap all fish products in aquafeed to boost sustainable fish farming
item.description: Global fish production and consumption have hit new heights, according to the United Nations. People worldwide are consuming much more fish per capita, and more than 23 million people now work in the aquaculture industry. That booming business is putting pressure on the world's oceans. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Outbursts from a Massive Star
item.description: Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star located in the galaxy shown in this image released on Nov. 9, 2026. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: HQ Web Team

item.title: Gemini and DECam showcase a young Type Ia supernova
item.description: A star's explosive demise has added a shiny new feature to NGC 1433, a barred spiral galaxy approximately 50 million light-years away in the southern constellation Horologium (the Pendulum Clock). New images of supernova SN 2026ahvu from the U.S. Department of Energy–fabricated Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and the Gemini South telescope capture the explosion against its galactic surroundings, recording an event that is changing in appearance from night to night. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Gemini Astronaut Photos Inspired Early Earth Observation Program
item.description: Astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. orbited Earth from November 11 to 15, 1966, on Gemini XII, the final mission of NASA’s Gemini program. In addition to successfully completing rendezvous maneuvers and spacewalks, procedures vital to sending American astronauts to the Moon, the crew was also spurring the development of […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Michele Ostovar

item.title: Direct observation of a submarine landslide reveals seafloor processes
item.description: Submarine landslides have significant implications for marine ecology and infrastructure, yet these unpredictable events have remained challenging to study. New research co-led by Newcastle University's Dr. Sanem Acikalin and involving an international team of collaborators from 10 institutions has provided the first direct observations of these elusive events. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study reveals mechanisms to sustain stable crop yields under long-term drip irrigation in arid regions
item.description: Combining drip irrigation during the growing season with autumn or winter irrigation can help control soil salinity and sustain high, stable crop yields in the arid regions of northwestern China, according to a new study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: WheatAI could speed wheat breeding and help farmers assess crops
item.description: Wheat researchers at South Dakota State University are perfecting an AI-powered web application designed to speed the work of wheat breeders and equip farmers with a more accurate tool for making decisions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fish prove every pregnancy is a battle: Unexpected evidence for the food fight between mothers and babies
item.description: Left to their own devices, babies in the womb would suck their mothers dry. A developing baby benefits from taking as many essential nutrients as possible, but evolutionary theory predicts that to survive pregnancy, mothers need to keep some of these nutrients for themselves. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Oregon logs its first H5N1 case in cows; farmers' union says human avian flu cases underreported in Washington
item.description: Earlier this week, the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (USDA's APHIS) announced the first detection of H5N1 avian flu in a dairy herd in Oregon. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Young green turtles find refuge in man-made lagoon in protected UAE wetland
item.description: A protected wetland in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) has become an oasis for young sea turtles, new research shows. The study tracked nine juvenile green turtles (shell length less than 60 cm (24 inches)) and found they were "highly resident" in the Al Qurm Wa Lehhfaiiah Protected Area—spending over 80% of their time there. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Las primeras reflexiones de la COP31 exhiben diferencias entre los países sobre la acción climática
item.description: Los organizadores de la COP31 de Turquía publicaron este 13 de noviembre un primer resumen de las prioridades de los diferentes países, que aglutinan posiciones muy diversas sobre los combustibles fósiles y la financiación, lo que augura una intensa negociación en la segunda semana. Entre las propuestas de este documento figura reafirmar el multilateralismo y el Acuerdo de París, así como responder a la prevista superación del umbral de 1,5 grados del calentamiento global. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24

item.title: Act now against El Niño or costs will double, UNDP warns
item.description: Acting now to counter the devastating effects of the El Niño phenomenon will cost half as much as waiting, the head of the U.N. Development Programme told AFP Friday. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Optical system maps multiple infrared fields onto one small detector
item.description: Researchers from the Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have developed an optical system that focuses light from several subfields onto a single small-format detector. By analyzing field-dependent spot shapes, the system identifies which subfield an isolated infrared target comes from. In sequence-level tests, it identified the correct field in about 89% of cases. The study is published in Optics and Laser Technology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Double axes and coarse pottery reveal connections across the Rhine 5,000 years ago
item.description: The Rhine, as the boundary between Western and Central Europe, appears to be a constant feature of European history. As early as the late fourth and early third millennia B.C., the traces of human activity east and west of the river differed. Archaeologists have long concluded that the river was a kind of barrier at that time, just as it has been in more recent centuries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Microscopic solar panels could help shape 3D-printed biological tissue
item.description: Bioprinting uses living cells and molecular signals to produce biological tissues and even whole organs, building them layer by layer in the lab. To keep the bioink, or blend of cells and materials that power this printing, correctly aligned to grow a target tissue, researchers use electricity. However, this typically requires bulky electronic interfaces and invasive wiring. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New research reveals when humor helps—and hurts—recruitment success
item.description: Humor is becoming an increasingly popular feature of job advertisements, with employers using it to stand out, capture attention and attract potential candidates. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Solving the space junk crisis isn't just about counting trash—it's about control and economics
item.description: If people ever think about cleaning up space debris, they typically think of something equivalent to a giant garbage truck in the sky, collecting lost astronaut tools and dead satellites, then hauling them back down to Earth to be deposited in a landfill. But dealing with space debris doesn't work that way, and a new paper by Dr. Slava Turyshev of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, available as a preprint on arXiv, makes a good argument as to why. We typically cover Turyshev for his work on the solar gravitational lens idea. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Oʻahu infrastructure threatened by tipping point in sea-level rise impacts
item.description: A new comprehensive study by researchers at the University of Hawaiʻi (UH) at Mānoa Climate Resilience Collaborative reveals that traditional sea-level rise models, which account only for rising ocean waters, drastically underestimate the true threat to coastal infrastructure on Oʻahu, Hawai'i. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A quarter of the world's reptiles use rocky habitats. So why aren't we protecting them?
item.description: Ask any reptile lover where to find a cold-blooded creature, and chances are they will point to a rocky outcrop. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wider daily temperature ranges linked to stronger fevers in amphibians and reptiles
item.description: When amphibians and reptiles get an infection, they sometimes raise their body temperature above its usual level by moving to a warmer environment. This well-documented behavioral response is known as behavioral fever. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Euclid's first data release: A stepping stone to its 3D map of the sky
item.description: The ESA's Euclid has already teased us with some early results. In the past, it's given us a small image covering 60 square degrees of the sky, created with a few days of observations. Those images showed individual targets from the Horsehead Nebula to the Perseus cluster of galaxies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover a hidden danger of viral infections that vaccines may prevent
item.description: A new study reveals that viral infections may leave behind hidden damage to the immune system long after symptoms disappear. Researchers found that mice recovering from an acute infection experienced lasting changes to their spleens and weakened immune responses, potentially leaving them more vulnerable to future threats. Surprisingly, prior vaccination completely prevented these harmful changes in the mouse model. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy
item.description: A study of more than 750,000 pregnancies found that early exposure to Ozempic, Wegovy, and similar drugs was not linked to increased pregnancy complications when used for weight loss, but was associated with a higher risk of premature birth when prescribed for diabetes. The surprising difference suggests that diabetes itself may be driving the risk, although researchers caution that the drugs' safety during pregnancy remains uncertain. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: How a multidrug-resistant bacterial clone emerged, evolved and disappeared in a hospital
item.description: Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium is listed by the World Health Organization as one of the highest-priority bacteria in its 2024 Bacterial Priority Pathogens List, ahead of MRSA, due to its ability to transfer resistance genes between humans, animals and the environment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Helping Montreal and other cities keep more institutional and commercial food waste out of the dump
item.description: Businesses and institutions in just 6% of Montreal's mapped area account for about 100,000 metric tons (110,000 tons) of food waste sent to landfill each year—half of the total amount from nonhousehold sources in the city as a whole, McGill University researchers found. Food service and retail businesses were found to be the biggest contributors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX va a intentar atrapar con unos brazos gigantes las dos partes de Starship. Nadie ha hecho algo así jamás
item.description: SpaceX está preparada hoy para hacer historia. Esta noche, 13 de noviembre de 2026, a las 22:45 GMT (23:45, hora peninsular española), está programado el vuelo 15 de Starship . No es un vuelo más, ya que con él pretende recuperar la primera etapa del cohete, como ha hecho varias veces, y después la segunda. Hasta ahora, ninguna agencia ni compañía espacial ha logrado recuperar un cohete completo; por lo que, si lo logra, será un hito que empujará a la empresa de Elon Musk muy por delante de sus competidoras. Dos etapas . Starship consta de dos etapas, el propulsor Super Heavy y la nave Ship… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Stopping statins after 70 may be safer than expected, but there's a catch
item.description: A major study of nearly 1,900 older adults suggests that stopping statins after age 70 may be relatively safe in the short term for people who have never experienced a heart attack or stroke. However, a higher rate of serious cardiovascular events or death during longer follow-up raises questions about the risks of discontinuing these widely prescribed medications. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Rocket Report: Starship set for historic test flight; a century of Electron
item.description: "You can simplify it as a big tank feeding engines." Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Eric Berger

item.title: Riders with disabilities face roadblocks when finding public transportation
item.description: A new national database developed at the University of Michigan shows that none of the top 99 public transportation systems in the United States are easy for people with disabilities to use in four key areas of accommodation and accessibility. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Superheated magma could fuel towering lava fountains
item.description: Why do some volcanoes erupt with spectacular lava fountains while others release lava more quietly? Scientists have discovered that a hidden effect of extreme heat inside magma may help explain the difference. Experiments revealed that superheated magma can delay crystal formation for more than eight hours, compared with just 20 minutes in magma that has not been superheated. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dark energy may have flipped from negative to positive 9.5 billion years ago
item.description: A mysterious force driving the expansion of the Universe may have undergone a dramatic reversal billions of years ago. Scientists exploring an overlooked branch of an alternative gravity theory discovered that dark energy could have switched from negative to positive roughly 9.5 billion years ago, potentially changing how we understand cosmic history. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: How career stakes shaped China's one-child policy enforcement
item.description: China's one-child policy is widely considered one of the most stringent public policies in modern history. Yet researchers have long debated how much it actually contributed to the country's dramatic fertility decline. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How a new ‘green energy corridor’ from the Caspian Sea could help Eastern Europe kick fossil fuels
item.description: The partnership signed at the COP31 climate summit aims to transform Azerbaijan into an interregional electricity hub. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: SpaceX Starship test to attempt first-ever spaceship 'catch'
item.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking "catch" of the spaceship following a day in orbit. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Dementia risk increases with number of cigarettes smoked per day
item.description: Researchers found that dementia risk increases with the number of cigarettes smoked per day, rising by 16% for those who smoke 10 a day and by 34% for those who smoke 20, compared with people who have never smoked. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: Light-activated molecules in porous crystals show potential for quantum chemical sensing
item.description: An international research team led by Nobuhiro Yanai from the University of Tokyo and Michael R. Wasielewski from Northwestern University has created polarized radical pairs, molecules with unpaired electrons whose spins align, in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), porous materials consisting of metal ions linked by organic molecules. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The Sun unleashed a monster storm. Earth may have made it worse
item.description: The massive solar storm that illuminated skies worldwide in May 2024 has uncovered an unexpected twist: Earth's own atmosphere may have helped make the storm so powerful. Satellite measurements revealed that roughly 85% of the charged particles fueling the disturbance originated from Earth's upper atmosphere rather than the solar wind. Scientists also detected an extraordinary 40% weakening of Earth's magnetic field high above the planet. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: An iconic puzzle comes home as production of the Rubik's Cube returns to Hungary
item.description: More than half a century ago, a Hungarian architect, sculptor and professor invented what would become one of the world's most popular and beloved puzzles whose appeal has spanned generations: the colorful, mind-bending, six-sided Rubik's Cube. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA crashed a spacecraft into an asteroid in 2022; Europe's Hera probe reaches impact site to investigate if Earth can be saved from space rocks
item.description: ESA's Hera spacecraft has initiated its observations of the Didymos asteroid system following NASA's DART mission's collision with Dimorphos. This investigation seeks to analyze the impact's effects on Dimorphos' structure and its trajectory, which is essential for planetary defense. Researchers aim to uncover the momentum enhancement factor and physical effects of the collision, while also deploying CubeSats for comprehensive data collection on both asteroids. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: This one single habit at night was linked to a 20 to 30 per cent higher rate of fatty liver disease and cirrhosis in a US study of nearly 200,000 adults followed for decades by Oregon researchers.
item.description: An intriguing study reveals that eating late at night can negatively impact liver health, contributing to greater risks of liver-related illnesses. Participants consuming late meals showed elevated instances of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and cirrhosis. By examining data from nearly 200,000 adults, researchers advocate for maintaining consistent meal timing to support the liver's functionality and align with natural bodily cycles. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
item.description: Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 13 – NGC 206 and the Star Clouds of Andromeda
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 13 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 206 […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: A Global Rebound for Mangroves
item.description: After decades of decline, this ecologically significant type of forest is making a comeback. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Children are not colorblind: Why early conversations about race are essential
item.description: Discussing racism with children can seem daunting to parents, caregivers and educators for several reasons. Often, it can feel uncomfortable talking about people's differences; conversations about racism reveal implicit biases and, for some, immense privilege. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers on 28 Peruvian cacao farms found birds and bats nearly doubled harvests by pest control
item.description: A recent study highlights the vital role of wildlife, particularly birds and bats, in managing pests on cacao farms. These creatures enhance cacao production, especially in areas rich in trees, leading to improved farmer profits. However, for farmers to maximize these benefits, preserving diverse habitats and effectively managing tree growth to ensure adequate light for cacao trees is essential. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: A dead star called J1328-1450 is circled by two separate rings of shattered planets
item.description: In a groundbreaking discovery, astronomers have identified two unique gaseous rings encircling the white dwarf star J1328-1450. Utilizing the Very Large Telescope in Chile, researchers explored the surrounding materials, indicating that some smaller planetary bodies likely survived the star's catastrophic end. Unlike previous findings, these rings display varied chemical compositions, shedding light on the planetary conditions that existed prior to the star's demise. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Research advances quantum computing that harnesses speed of light
item.description: Quantum computers have the potential to perform calculations more quickly than supercomputers, but they could be even faster and more energy-efficient if they were built with photons as their basic units, called qubits. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Automated assembly in space is the future and NOM4D is showing the way
item.description: If we want big things in space, we'll have to build and assemble them there. Rocket fairings are not large enough to accommodate the large things we want to have in space. Not only that, but the stubborn rocket equation refuses to bend itself to our desires. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The moon is not the Wild West: Experts call for a pause on lunar industrialization
item.description: As the major powers and the private companies go full tilt with their plans to develop infrastructure and extract resources on the moon, the questions around environmental protection, international regulation and who benefits all come into play. Vilnius University Institute of International Relations and Political Science (VU IIRPS) professor Florian Rabitz, together with Xiao-Shan Yap from Utrecht University, explores these concerns in their research article, "Don't Fly Me to the Moon: A Moratorium on Lunar Industrialization," published in the journal Global Environmental Politics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: UN climate summit pushes electrification goal as groups call for mining safeguards
item.description: The pledge builds on commitments made at previous UN climate summits: At COP28, countries agreed to work toward tripling renewable energy capacity and transitioning away from fossil fuels. COP29 focused on energy storage, grid modernisation and climate finance Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Trusted online information may help networking skills translate into startup ambitions, survey suggests
item.description: A study of almost 200 undergraduate and postgraduate students in South Korea suggests that the skills of aspiring entrepreneurs are more likely to translate into plans to start a business when supported by trustworthy digital networks and useful online resources. Details of the findings are reported in the World Review of Entrepreneurship, Management and Sustainable Development. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue
item.description: Researchers have uncovered a surprising hidden function of a protein that may hold the key to repairing damaged muscles and treating muscular dystrophy. Known for protecting chromosomes, TRF2 also helps muscle stem cells maintain their identity and regenerate injured tissue. When scientists removed the protein in mice, muscles struggled to repair themselves, and muscular dystrophy progressed dramatically faster. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Vision and interferometry improve calibration of large monolithic mirrors
item.description: In a new study published in Measurement, researchers from the Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have developed a calibration method that combines machine vision with interferometry. This method separates a mirror's fixed internal offset from changes in the test path alignment. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A breakthrough in magnetism could make AI chips use dramatically less energy
item.description: Researchers at Brown University have overcome a major obstacle to creating ultra-low-power computer chips that could help slash the energy demands of AI. Their breakthrough eliminates a long-standing "dead layer" problem that causes promising materials to stop working when made extremely thin. Remarkably, the new technique not only preserves the materials' electrical and magnetic properties at nearly atomic thicknesses but also gives them enhanced magnetic capabilities Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Black rhinos are mostly loners, but not always: Why this matters for saving the species
item.description: Black rhinos are notoriously aggressive, not just to humans but also to their fellow black rhinos. Aggression is so prevalent that injuries sustained after fighting with another black rhino are a common cause of death. Because of this aggression and their solitary nature, black rhino social behavior has been largely unexplored. Yet it may be key to conservation of this critically endangered African icon. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Early signs of stock market instability may appear in how traders place orders
item.description: The influence of financial markets cannot be overstated, and this influence highlights the need for thorough market analysis. However, being thorough can be difficult when markets are highly complex and ever-changing, prompting the search for a suitable approach to analysis. Fortunately, the increasing availability of detailed market data, together with advances in mathematical theories, offers new opportunities to better understand market behavior. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Magnetic nanoparticles cut adhesive curing from 24 hours to one in laboratory tests
item.description: Scientists at Nanyang Technological University, Singapore (NTU Singapore) and global automotive supplier Motherson are collaborating to develop a magnetic heating technology that could significantly reduce the time and energy needed to cure industrial coatings. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Robotic tools help unlock the hidden microbial world of the deep sea
item.description: Scientists have developed a robotic system that can recreate the extreme conditions of the deep ocean in the laboratory, opening up access to some microorganisms for the first time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Animal vs. plant protein reveals a surprising testosterone divide
item.description: A surprising new study suggests that where men get their protein may be linked to their testosterone levels. Researchers studying more than 2,500 men found that higher animal protein intake, particularly from dairy, was associated with lower testosterone, while plant protein was linked to higher levels. The findings raise intriguing questions about how everyday food choices might relate to male hormone levels. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Using AI to predict how bioplastics behave under heat
item.description: A new ANIPH study shows how machine learning models can predict how PHB and PHBV respond to heat, helping manufacturers design formulations that are easier to process. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Earth's orbital asymmetries share recurring rhythms with El Niño, study finds
item.description: Every few years, an unusual warming of surface waters across the central and eastern tropical Pacific—known as El Niño—reorganizes atmospheric circulation worldwide, bringing severe droughts to some continents and torrential rainfall to others. For decades, oceanographers and meteorologists have mapped the intricate internal machinery behind the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), from shifting trade winds to subsurface ocean waves. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Engineered atomic interactions help microwave sensor capture three times as much information
item.description: Researchers from the Faculty of Physics at the University of Warsaw (UW) and the Center for Optical Quantum Technologies at the University of Warsaw's Center for New Technologies (CeNT UW) have developed a method for ultrasensitive microwave sensing. Using cold, strongly interacting Rydberg atoms as a microwave detector, the researchers observed that carefully engineered interactions between the atoms make the atomic state resistant to loss. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Advocates warn FIFO standards are slipping on mine sites
item.description: Researchers say minimum accommodation standards are dropping on mine sites, despite years of public scrutiny and industry reports. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Alistair Bates and Bryn Wakefield

item.title: Not afraid of ghosts: Curiosity and fearlessness apparent in German shepherd genes
item.description: German shepherd dogs bred for working are more curious and less neurotic than German shepherds bred for show. A new study from Uppsala University and the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences has shown that the differences are not only apparent in the dogs' behavior, but also in their genes. In previous studies, similar genes in humans have been associated with neuroticism. The research is published in the journal Animal Genetics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Global climate policies continue to advance despite setbacks, research finds
item.description: The latest findings from the Oxford Climate Policy Monitor, led by the Blavatnik School of Government and the Oxford Sustainable Law Programme, show that progress in Asia, Africa and Latin America is more than offsetting the weakening or reversal of climate policies in parts of Europe and North America. Fuente: Phys.org.
